releases.title: Aberdeen Destination Marketing, Development and Convention Bureau Service
releases.description:
Aberdeen City Council is seeking to appoint a single contractor to provide an integrated, city-focused Destination Marketing, Development and Convention Bureau Service for Aberdeen.
The Service will support the objectives of the Aberdeen Visitor Levy and the sustainable growth of Aberdeen’s visitor economy. It will include destination marketing and communications, destination development, travel-trade activity, visitor information and welcome services, visitor-economy business engagement, Convention Bureau services, administration of a ring-fenced Convention Bureau Subvention Fund, research, evaluation, data and performance reporting.
The Contract will be for an initial period of three years, with an option for the Council to extend it by up to a further two years. The anticipated commencement date is 1 April 2027.

Scottish Water Horizons is seeking to appoint contractors to provide transport of wastewater services across Scotland. The materials likely to be required for transport are non-hazardous liquid from commercial and industrial clients including:
• landfill leachate
• other liquid non-hazardous waste
• septic waste and sewage

lots.description:
Scottish Water Horizons is seeking to appoint contractors to provide transport of wastewater services across Scotland. The materials likely to be required for transport are non-hazardous liquid from commercial and industrial clients including:
• landfill leachate
• other liquid non-hazardous waste
• septic waste and sewage

Contractors will be expected to pay due regard to all applicable legal requirements relevant to the provision of wastewater transport services. The vehicles will all be articulated tankers.

The barrels must be suitable for carrying landfill leachate. However, there may be occasions when a rigid tanker is required for smaller jobs, although this will be infrequent but successful suppliers will be required to have the flexibility. Additional information: https://atamis-scottishwater.my.salesforce-sites.com/ProSpend__CS_PublicLandingPage?SearchType=Projects

lots.title: Hard FM M&E Central
lots.description: The Authority is seeking to put in place a Hard FM contract for the provision of Lot 1 – M&E Central. The delivery of Mechanical and Electrical (M&E) services comprises of the planned and reactive maintenance, repair, replacement, testing, and management of building engineering systems. Planned services ensure assets remain safe, compliant, and operational through scheduled maintenance activities, while reactive services provide timely response to unforeseen failures and emergencies to restore service continuity and protect building operations.

lots.title: Hard FM M&E North Scotland

Planned services ensure assets remain safe, compliant, and operational through scheduled maintenance activities, while reactive services provide timely response to unforeseen failures and emergencies to restore service continuity and protect building operations.

releases.title: Independent Children's Advocacy Service
releases.description:
Dumfries and Galloway Council (the Purchaser) wishes to commission children's advocacy services that:
- are independent and professional;
- provide individual (one-to-one) advocacy that is issue focused; and
- meet statutory requirements and Scottish Executive priorities.
The service will covers such services under the following categories:
- Advocacy services for children and young people who are or have been looked after and accommodated within or outwith the region (excluding those who are placed locally by another Local Authority) up until the age of 26.
- Advocacy for children and young people on the Child Protection Register.
- Advocacy for children and young people in terms of the Mental Health (Care and Treatment) (Scotland) Act 2003.

lots.description:
This procurement is to obtain a suitable advocacy service provider for children's advocacy services. The service objectives are as follows:
To provide an independent and confidential advocacy service to include information, support and advice for Dumfries and Galloway children and young people who are or have been looked after and accommodated within or outwith the region.
To provide access to an advocacy service for children & young people regardless of age, gender, disability, sexual orientation, ethnic origin, faith/religion, or social background.
To match service users and advocates appropriate to each situation’s needs, seeking specialist support where indicated and ensuring service users comfort at all times.
To ensure that children & young people’s own views are heard and adequately represented.
To provide advocacy, related support and information in an age-appropriate and child/young person-centred manner.
To help children and young people to access and understand information relevant to them and make appropriate choices or decisions which give them fuller control of their lives.
To promote choices to young people.
To support children & young people who, because of incapacity or communication difficulties, may not be able to express their needs or views.
To provide advocacy for children and young people who have a mental disorder in compliance with the Mental Health Act.
To guide children and young people towards self-advocacy and avoid creation of dependency.
To develop links with service providers, professionals and relevant support organisations to ensure clear understanding of the role of advocacy.
To develop and promote children and young people’s involvement in service planning.

releases.title: PKC14238  Central Heating Upgrade Phase 6
releases.description:
Perth & Kinross Council (‘the Council’) is seeking to appoint suitably qualified and experienced contractors to carry out central heating life cycle replacement works on PKC’s domestic tenanted properties.
The works comprise of the like-for-like replacement of gas boilers and radiators, full gas boiler systems inclusive of radiators and pipework; replacement of electric storage and panel heating systems, as well as the replacement of existing storage heating, electric wet boilers, and solid fuel heating with Air Source Heat Pumps. This list is not exhaustive. The full scope of works will be set out in the Employer’s Requirements within the tender documentation.

releases.title: Flexible Framework for Early Learning and Childcare Services in North Lanarkshire 2027-2031
releases.description: In accordance with The Public Contracts (Scotland) Regulations 2015, Regulation 74, North Lanarkshire Council intends to establish a Flexible Framework for the provision of funded Early Learning and Childcare (ELC) services. The Framework will enable the Council to supplement its internal ELC provision through external providers and support delivery of the statutory funded ELC entitlement. The proposed Framework will be for 4 years, with options for Tenderers to apply to the Framework in either years 1, 2, 3 or 4.

lots.description:
The primary service requirement is the delivery of funded early learning and childcare placements, providing eligible children up to 1140 hours of funded early learning and childcare per year.
.
A detailed specification is contained within the invitation to tender (“ITT”) pack which is accessible and downloadable from the Supplier Attachment Area within the PCS-Tendering system.
.
Service delivery must be carried out in accordance with the information provided within this Contract Notice, the ITT Documents and the Council's Framework Agreement. Additional information: PLEASE BE AWARE OF THE EXCLUSION GROUNDS:
Economic operators may be excluded from this competition if they are in any of the situations referred to in regulation 58 of the Public Contracts (Scotland) Regulations 2015.

releases.title: PKC14238  Central Heating Upgrade Phase 6
releases.description:
Perth & Kinross Council (‘the Council’) is seeking to appoint suitably qualified and experienced contractors to carry out central heating life cycle replacement works on PKC’s domestic tenanted properties.
The works comprise of the like-for-like replacement of gas boilers and radiators, full gas boiler systems inclusive of radiators and pipework; replacement of electric storage and panel heating systems, as well as the replacement of existing storage heating, electric wet boilers, and solid fuel heating with Air Source Heat Pumps. This list is not exhaustive. The full scope of works will be set out in the Employer’s Requirements within the tender documentation.

This equipment will be utilised to study materials and devices and circuits transport and electronic behaviour at low temperature and under a magnetic field
Please refer to the PURCH3086 - Invitation to Tender document for additional information and specification.

releases.title: Short Breaks for Children and Young People with Disabilities aged 5 to 17 years old in Norfolk Framework Agreement
releases.description: The Council wishes to commission a range of high quality, outcome-focused, inclusive Short Breaks for children and young people with disabilities (CWD) aged 5 to 17 years who live in Norfolk, to support its vision to provide opportunities where children and young people with disabilities can thrive, grow, achieve, and have fun in the community with their peers, whilst supporting their families to have a break from caring. Ensuring Short Breaks provide the right opportunities, at the right time, in the right place, for the right groups and individuals is key to achieving our vision.  The Framework commenced on the 1st of April 2023, and this is the fifth opening to allow new applicants to apply to be on the framework.

releases.buyer: COUNTESS OF CHESTER HOSPITAL NHS FOUNDATION TRUST
releases.title: National Framework Agreement for the provision of Sexual Health Services
releases.description:
The demand for accessible, high-quality and innovative sexual health services continues to evolve in response to changing population needs, advances in clinical practice, increasing digital delivery models and the ongoing focus on reducing health inequalities.
The Framework will provide Relevant Authorities with a fully compliant route for the provision of sexual health services, supporting the commissioning of integrated, digital, clinical, diagnostic, prevention, outreach and specialist support services. The Framework is designed to enable Contracting Authorities to secure services that improve public health outcomes, promote early intervention and prevention, support vulnerable populations, and ensure equitable access to care. 
The overall aim of the Framework is to provide a compliant route to market facilitating the procurement of various Sexual Health Services. 
The Framework has been established under The Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023 and The Health Services (Provider Selection Regime) (Wales) Regulations 2025 (and as amended) (together the PSR) for use by all Relevant Authorities (and any future successors to these organisations).
"Relevant Authority" is defined in section 12ZB(7) of the National Health Service Act 2006 and in section 10A(9) of the National Health Service (Wales) Act 2006. It means a combined authority, an integrated care board, a local authority in England, NHS England, an NHS foundation trust or an NHS trust established under section 25 of the National Health Service Act 2006, a county council or county borough council in Wales, a local health board established under section 11 of the National Health Service (Wales) Act 2006, a National Health Service trust established under section 18 of the National Health Service (Wales) Act 2006, or a special health authority established under section 22 of the National Health Service (Wales) Act 2006. 
For the avoidance of doubt, any successor bodies of any of the above entities shall be entitled to place Orders and shall be deemed Relevant Authorities for the purposes of this Framework.
The Framework will be re-opened to new applicants every two years, approximately 90 days before the anniversary of the Framework Commencement Date.

releases.title: Provision of Security and physical guarding services
releases.description: PSD Scotland are seeking to put in place a contract for the provision of security and physical guarding services.

lots.title: Security and physical guarding - East
lots.description:
Public Services Delivery (PSD) Scotland are seeking to put in place a Security and physical guarding contract for the east of Scotland, sites include Gyle Square, Jack Copland Centre, Norseman House. The contract start date will be 1st April 2027 and the estimated value per annum is 300,000 GBP.
Services will include;
Delivery of reactive security services, dependent on site requirements and operating arrangements.
Initial interrogation and investigation of fire alarm panel activations, with escalation where required.
Locking and unlocking of premises, dependent on site requirements.
Management of building security, including access and egress control.
Provision of basic reception and customer service functions, including directing visitors and responding to enquiries where appropriate.

Services will include;
Delivery of reactive security services, dependent on site requirements and operating arrangements.
Initial interrogation and investigation of fire alarm panel activations, with escalation where required.
Locking and unlocking of premises, dependent on site requirements.
Management of building security, including access and egress control.
Provision of basic reception and customer service functions, including directing visitors and responding to enquiries where appropriate.
